entries.text: Firstborn son is to receive the father's birthright.
Illegitimate children not to receive birthright.
Blessings to be bestowed on the heir of the family.
Birthright of the firstborn can be sold to another son .
A greater portion of the father's inheritance to be given to the firstborn son.
Primary part of inheritance to go to firstborn son rather than a favored son.
Houses and riches are given as an inheritance from a father.
Land ownership can pass by inheritance.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children.
Daughters are to receive an inheritance from their father when he has no son.
If a man has no children his inheritance is given to his brothers.
If a man has no children or brothers then his inheritance is given to his father's brethren or his nearest family kin.
Birthright of firstborn son can be lost and given up to another son if the firstborn commits a sin against the family.

When a man dies having no children and his widow marries her husband's brother, the son she bears by him shall succeed in the name of the brother which is dead and shall have his birthright and inheritance.
A will and testament is in force after a man is dead, for it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
A heir, as long as he is a child, is under guardians until the time prescribed by his father that he is to inherit.
